ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a schematic of a right triangle and its incircle and circumcircle, consistent with the description in the question stem. According to the question stem, a and b are the two shorter sides of the right triangle, that is, the two legs. Let the hypotenuse be c, then c = sqrt(a^2+b^2). The diameter of the circumcircle of a right triangle is equal to the hypotenuse, so the diameter of the circumcircle is c. The formula for the radius of the incircle of a right triangle is r = (a+b-c)/2, therefore the diameter of the incircle is 2r = a+b-c. Adding the two gives (a+b-c)+c = a+b.

method.method_draft: Use standard radius formulas for a right triangle. Read from the text that the two shorter sides are the legs, so the hypotenuse is c = sqrt(a^2+b^2). The circumcircle of a right triangle has diameter equal to the hypotenuse, so its diameter is c. The inradius of a right triangle is r = (a+b-c)/2, hence the incircle diameter is 2r = a+b-c. Add the two diameters: (a+b-c)+c = a+b.
